title: Grammar lexer adaptor and streaming framing for tool-call boundaries
author: Priya Shah
description: Context: We've seen several production incidents where function/tool call frames were split across streaming chunks due to tokenizer boundary mismatches when constrained decoders applied grammar or regex-based filters. This caused downstream tool-call parsers to drop arguments or mis-attribute return markers. Motivation: Make constrained decoding backends (CFG and regex) resilient to tokenizer-driven split points and stabilize the streaming framing for tool/function calls, without regressing latency or throughput.

a9c8f11: add streaming-framing state machine to ensure tool-call envelope continuity

review_comments: Evan Park: Please explain why the lexer layer is preferable to patching the regex backend — are there perf implications?

Priya Shah: The lexer adapts existing CFG grammars into a token-aware pattern that avoids re-scanning full byte streams; microbenchmarks show ~2% throughput regression at p99 throughput but eliminates class of parse-errors. Added benchmark results in PR.
Marta López: Tests look thorough but can we add a short network jitter simulation to the reassembly tests?
Priya Shah: Added jitter scenarios to streaming/reassembly_tests.rs and a CI job that runs them under qemu-user network emulation (kept disabled by default; enabled in canary pipeline).
Noah Kim: A couple of nits on doc wording for the openai-compat shim and suggested clarifying migration steps for customers.
Priya Shah: Updated docs/api/structured-output.md with migration notes and sample config.
release_notes: Stabilize streaming framing for function/tool calls when using constrained decoding backends. Adds a grammar-lexer adaptor to align CFG/regex constraints with tokenizer boundaries, improves compatibility with the OpenAI-compatible tool-call envelope, and includes regressions tests and canary configs.
